correctness.rationale: Exact hypothesis is surjective initial-interval height-words, counting all cyclic output words once up to rotation, without letter permutations. The original overlap graph is Eulerian by the cited 2012 proof. Every incomplete prefix has uniquely forced next letter; rotations of any original complete edge lead within at most n steps to a complete prefix, so all forced corridors terminate and contraction bijects cyclic Euler tours, including parallel arcs. Every core prefix has outdegree max+2, giving the explicit Stirling factorial product. The standard BEST and directed matrix–tree theorems give the 1-root-normalized cyclic count. The 75-vertex reduced cofactor at n=5 and the 13-vertex cofactor at n=4 were computed using exact Bareiss, independently regenerated by modular/CRT under Hadamard bounds; order-four full graph and eight order-three cycles separately corroborate. Complete 541-edge path certificate is checked. No finite test is used to infer an unproved general determinant formula.

evidence: The BEST theorem applies to every connected Eulerian digraph, so its general determinant-product framework is established. Sawada–Gabrić §2 describes enumeration of all Euler tours and weak-order sampling in §4.2. Sawada et al. §5.3 constructs a particular cycle.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general graph theorems and enumerator directly imply an algorithm for producing this finite invariant, and are credited. They do not provide the special forced-core reduction or evaluate the 13- and 75-vertex cofactors. The exact order-four/five counts are not direct statements of those broader results, although reproducible applications of them.

originality.rationale: The all-tour determinants at orders four and five and the evaluated cyclic counts were not found in the four inspected primary full texts or relevant public numerical tables. Horan–Hurlbert prove existence, Sawada–Wong and Sawada et al. give construction, and Sawada–Gabrić give general all-tour generation and sampling; that general algorithm and BEST are prior work, not new contributions. Exact stated finite cardinalities require evaluated input-specific determinants and a complete forced-corridor contraction. Own accessible ledger claims were separately checked for semantic overlap. Unindexed prior computational counts remain a genuine priority risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed prior census of all weak-order universal cycles might have evaluated the same determinants, despite not appearing in inspected primary papers, searchable records or the checked OEIS entries.
The historical Diaconis–Graham discussion (2008) was not independently inspected in full; later authors characterize it as addressing existence rather than all-tour enumeration.
A general Euler-tour generator from 2025 may permit independent recomputation; it does not itself state these evaluated values.

value.rationale: The complete number of distinct cyclic universal schedules is a natural invariant that measures ambiguity/multiplicity beyond the known existence and generator algorithms. The order-four and order-five evaluated cardinalities are new finite exact data not implied numerically by the previously examined source claims. Degree-one-corridor contraction proves a structural simplification for the entire family and reduces the largest evaluated matrix from 308 to 75 vertices, enabling reproducible large-integer enumeration. The value is the natural all-cycle census and compression, not a claim to improve a textbook Euler-tour algorithm or to provide a paper-sized all-order asymptotic theory.
